topics.core_competency: The learner understands the basic parts of a plant and their functions; appreciates the growth requirements of crop plants, and grows cereals successfully.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: explain the ways in which crops are important to humans (k,u, a,v)
understand the structures and functions of the basic parts of a plant(u)
understand the structures and functions of the parts of the reproductive system of a plant (k, u ,v)
understand the factors that influence plant growth and crop production (k,u,s, a,v)
show skills in classifying crops as annual, biennial and perennial (u,s, a,v)
understand the value of cereals both in nutritional terms and as a commodity (k, u, a,v)
understand how to select appropriate planting material for the cereal chosen for growing (k,u, a,v)
show skills in growing cereals(s)
show skill in maintaining soil fertility in cereals (k, u,s, a,v)
show skills in handling cereals during and after harvest (s, a,v)
understand the various methods for storing cereals (k, u, a,v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups or as a class, learners brainstorm and record the ways in which crops are important to humans and the value of cereals, both in terms of nutrition and as a commodity.
In groups, learners examine and draw the different basic parts of plants, including the reproductive system. Research and annotate diagrams to explain the functions of each part.

In groups, learners research, discuss and, prepare a presentation on: the meaning of annual, biennial and perennial plants; examples of crop plants that are annuals, biennials and perennials; the propagation methods that are used for each

In groups, learners plan, carry out, and record the outcome of an investigation into the effect of wind/temperature on plants by conducting a simple experiment; using two identical well-watered pot plants, a fan/a heater or cooler, a thermometer and weighing scales.

Individually or in pairs, learners conduct an investigation to compare the growth of plants in different conditions in the outdoor environment, considering factors such as rainfall, light, temperature, and humidity.

In groups or as a class practical, learners select which cereal to grow, select and sow seeds or other planting material, care for and manage the growing crop, maintain soil fertility, harvest the crop, select, and use appropriate techniques for storing the seeds. Individuals keep records at each stage in the process and produce a report. Individuals shares how you can earn as or feed a family when growing cereals

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners carrying out activities and intervene as necessary to ensure learning is taking place by, like offering groups guidance with research strategies; supporting groups to ensure use of scientific techniques in investigations; checking all individuals understand key points from presentations; highlighting and demonstrating good practice in terms of use of tools, care for crops, etc.
Listen to pair and group discussions, asking probing questions and offering guidance to ensure that all individuals think critically, develop skills, and understanding of cereals.

Evaluate learning through quality of products: reports on importance of crops and value of cereals; annotated diagrams of plant parts and their functions; presentations on plant life cycles and propagation of examples; investigation reports; crop yield (quality and quantity) and reports on process.

topics.core_competency: The learner grows and processes root and stem tubers for the market

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the meanings and the value of roots and stem tubers, both in terms of nutrition and as a commodity (u, a,v)
understand how to select appropriate planting material for the crop chosen for growing (k,u, a,v)
show skills in growing roots/stem tubers (s, a,v)
show skill in handling roots/stem tubers during and after harvest (s, a,v)
show skill in processing and solar drying of roots/stem tubers (k, s, a,v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: As a class or in groups, learners brainstorm, research and report on the meaning of tubers, root and stem, giving examples of each and their value in the diet and as marketable commodities.
Groups use their findings to select a root or stem tuber to grow and harvest and report the reasons for their choice verbally or in writing.

In groups or as a whole class practical, learners select appropriate planting material for their chosen crop, plant the crop, care for and manage the crop as it grows, maintain soil fertility, harvest the crop, select and use appropriate methods for processing the crop, using solar drying accordingly. Individuals keep records at each stage in the process and produce a report.
As a group, learners select, design and construct a solar dryer for proper processing (sorting, cleaning and washing) of root and stem tubers, and present their product to the class.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they carry out the activities, intervening if required to ensure that they are on track with research and that they understand how to use tools and equipment effectively and safely in root and stem tuber growing. Observe as they select, design, construct, and operate a solar dryer, focusing on; participation, collaboration, time management, creativity, adhering to standard measurements, and justification for actions.
Listen to learners’ conversations and contribute as necessary to guide and ensure that all make progress towards achievement of learning outcomes.

Evaluate products: reports on root and stem tubers, examples and their value; explanations of choice of tuber to grow and reasons; crop yield (quality and quantity); effectiveness of processing after harvest and of solar dryers.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: know the structure of a seed and understand the functions of each part (k,u)
show skills in breaking seed dormancy in crops and optimising germination (s, u)
understand the value of legumes and oil seeds in both nutritional and financial terms (k, u, a,v)
understand how to select appropriate seeds for growing a chosen crop (u, k, s, a,v)
show skills in growing legumes and oil seeds (s, a,v)
show skill in handling legumes and oil seeds during and after harvest(s , a,v)
know, understand, and apply the skills involved in the various methods of storing legumes and oil seeds (k, u, s, a,v)

must_cover: Value of legumes and oil seeds

suggested_learning_activities.description: In pairs, learners: a. examine, discover, and draw the internal structure of a seed; b. research the functions of each part of the seed and the types of seed dormancy; c. complete a report on seed structure, and dormancy

In groups, learners: a. brainstorm the meanings and think of examples of legumes and oilseeds; b. research the nutritional and financial value of legumes and oilseeds; c. complete a chart on legumes and oil seeds, giving important examples and explaining their value

In groups, learners select appropriate seeds for growing a chosen crop through an experiment using, like., a seed viability test (Tetrazolium salt and potassium permanganate), and calculate the germination percentage and report on their findings verbally and/or in writing
In groups, learners prepare the ground, plant seeds, grow, care for and manage a legume or an oil seed crop through to harvest, recording lessons learned throughout the process
In groups, learners research, put into practice and report upon hygienic methods of drying and storing harvested legumes and oilseeds

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe pairs and groups, monitoring learning and intervening as appropriate to ensure that all learners are fully engaged and making progress towards success in terms of learning outcomes.

Listen carefully to learners’ discussions, asking questions to prompt critical thinking and creative solutions to challenges in legume/oil seed growing and storage. Guide learners to help them overcome barriers to learning.

Evaluate quality of learning through the quality of the products: drawings and reports on seeds, legume/oil seed charts, seed viability reports, crop yield (quality and quantity), seed drying and storage reports.

themes.theme_description: Rearing and marketing of domestic animals.

topics.core_competency: The learner rears and markets a domestic animal profitably.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: identify different types of farm/farmed animals and their purpose (k,u,v)
understand the value of rearing domestic animals both in terms of their contribution to the human diet and as a commodity through which farmers make a living (k, a,v)
understand how to select an animal to rear (u,s, a,v)
understand the basics of caring for domestic animals, including the nutrient and feed requirements and provision of water (k, u, a,v)
show skills needed to keep farm animals in a healthy state (u,s, a,v)
understand the types of housing for different animals and the reasons for the designs, and show skills in constructing an animal house (u,s, a,v)
understand the digestive and reproductive system of ruminants and non-ruminant animals,( a,v)
understand the significance of animal feeding programs (u,v)
know how to conserve and use feeding resources (k, s,v)
understand how to prepare fodder grass and crops for feeding animals (u,s,v)
understand the importance of planned animal breeding and selection (k,u)

must_cover: Types of farm animals and purpose

suggested_learning_activities.description: As a class, learners visit a nearby farm to observe the different species and breeds of available farm animals, taking note of their characteristics and how their needs are provided for on the farm.

In groups, learners discuss with the farmer he different methods of caring for these animals, the challenges faced, and the value of the animals in financial and nutritional terms. Individually, learners complete a report on the animals seen and the advantages and disadvantages of rearing each.
In pairs, learners discuss their thoughts on which would be the best animal to rear and why, and share their ideas with the rest of the class.

In pairs, learners practice and demonstrate skills in aspects of caring for animals (depending on the animals chosen/available), such as: selecting a breed for breeding, feeding, watering, catching, and bringing down larger animals, leading larger animals, exhibiting for a show, and calculating age, checking health, dosing with medicines, and immunizing, dehorning, ear tagging, and castrating male animals
In groups, learners research the characteristics of good quality animal housing, practice, and demonstrate practical skills in construction

In groups, learners dissect a domestic animal, such as a goat, a rabbit or a hen, displaying and labelling the main parts of the digestive and reproductive systems and giving the main functions of each

In groups, learners research the source of feeds, nutrient composition, and how to formulate a ration. How to store feeds safely, how to prepare fodder grass, and other crops for feeding animals. Groups present findings in a table or poster chart.
In groups, learners research the meaning and importance of selective breeding.
Groups prepare a presentation for the class to explain how selective breeding could improve yields from a farmed animal of their choice.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Listen to learners’ conversations and contribute as necessary to guide and ensure all make progress towards achievement of learning outcomes.

Observe learners identify different species and breeds of animals; discuss the different methods of caring for animals and guide them on how to select the best animal to rear; dissect and identify the parts of the digestive and reproductive systems of named animals; focus on supporting learners on feeding, watering, restraining, dosing animals, vaccinating, dehorning, castrating, ear tagging, slaughtering animals, preparing animal feeds, feed ration computation and constructing animal housing structures, how selective breeding can help to improve yields in animals

Evaluate the product selecting a breed for rearing; the animal husbandry practices of –feeding, watering, restraining, dosing animals, vaccinating, dehorning, castrating, ear tagging, slaughtering animals, preparing animal feeds and constructed animal housing structures

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: Choose one of the following domestic animals to rear: poultry, goats, fish or rabbits

topics.core_competency: The learner rears and markets a domestic animal profitably.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand and identify the important breeds of poultry reared in Uganda and their place in supplying the market (u,s)
understand how eggs are hatched and ways of raising chickens (u,s)
know how to care for the health of poultry and understand the role of veterinary services (k, u, a,v)
demonstrate knowledge of diseases and pests affecting poultry (k, s ,a)
demonstrate the use of tools and equipment for controlling diseases and pests in poultry (s, a,v)
show skill in handling poultry and its products (s, a,v)
understand how to market animal products (u, s, a,v)
understand the importance of and demonstrate entrepreneurial skills in marketing poultry (u, s,a)
apply knowledge and skills related to the marketing of animals and their products (k, s, a,v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups or as a class, learners brainstorm and research on the different breeds and their commercial importance in supplying the demand for eggs and poultry meat in Uganda. Individuals record conclusions.

In groups, learners watch a video clip, visit a poultry farm or use other resources to research on how eggs are hatched and chickens are reared commercially for meat and for egg laying. Learners report their findings to the class.

In groups, learners apply their skills and understanding in practice, from egg incubation through to marketing both meat and eggs. This includes incubating eggs, hatching, and brooding. Growing birds, debeaking, and vaccinating, feeding rations, finishing off for the market, as well as weighing animals, slaughtering, and grading, branding and packaging cut carcasses, caring for layers, egg collection, washing, grading and marketing. Individuals keep learning logs and record lessons learned throughout the process.

As a class or in groups, learners research common pests and diseases, their causes, symptoms, and treatment. These conditions include: Newcastle disease, fowl pox, fowl typhoid, salmonella, Marek’s disease, coccidiosis, mites, lice, fleas, and worms. Then learners present findings in a table
Individually, learners practise using tools and equipment such as a drenching gun for controlling diseases and pests in poultry.
As a class, learners discuss and record conclusions on the role of farmers in prevention and treatment of pests and diseases and circumstances in which veterinary services need to be involved.
As a class, learners observe a demonstration of the slaughtering and dressing of chickens (poultry) for sale, practise as appropriate, and write a summary of the process.
In groups, learners research on the marketing policies and rules that apply to animals and animal products and then develop a plan for marketing their animals and animal products.
As a class, learners discuss and explore the different entrepreneurial skills needed in poultry farming and write a list of the characteristics of an ideal poultry farmer.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Listen to learners’ conversations and contribute as necessary to guide and ensure that all make progress towards achievement of learning outcomes.

Observe learners as they carry out the activities, intervening if required to ensure that they are on track with up to date research information available and that they understand how to use tools and equipment effectively and safely in poultry rearing. Focusing on; participation, collaboration, time management, creativity, adhering to standard measurements, and justification for actions taken.

Evaluate products: hatching of eggs; commercial rearing of chicken for meat or eggs; growing of birds; on husbandry practices of brooding, debeaking, vaccinating, feeding rations, slaughtering of birds for sale; egg yield and handling (quality and quantity); marketing; research of common poultry pests, parasites and diseases ; using tools and equipment in poultry rearing. Research work on the different kinds of endo-parasites and ecto- parasites that affect poultry.

practicals.title: Poultry Rearing Practice
practicals.description_verbatim: In groups, learners apply their skills and understanding in practice, from egg incubation through to marketing both meat and eggs. This includes incubating eggs, hatching, and brooding. Growing birds, debeaking, and vaccinating, feeding rations, finishing off for the market, as well as weighing animals, slaughtering, and grading, branding and packaging cut carcasses, caring for layers, egg collection, washing, grading and marketing.

practicals.title: Slaughtering and dressing of chickens
practicals.description_verbatim: As a class, learners observe a demonstration of the slaughtering and dressing of chickens (poultry) for sale, practise as appropriate, and write a summary of the process.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: know and understand terminology relating to fish farming and aquaponics (k,u)
understand why fish farming is important in Uganda and the value of fish, both in nutritional terms and as a commercial product (u, k, a,v)
know how to select appropriate fish for rearing (k, s, a,v)
understand how a fish pond is constructed and how to determine whether the soil in a given area is suitable for a pond (u, v, s)
construct a fixed pond or a mobile pond/aquaponic system or an aquarium (u,s,v)
understand how to, and show skills in, stocking and managing a fish pond and/ or an aquaponic system (u,s, a,v)
recognise and understand how to deal with different diseases, parasites, and predators (k,u, a,v)
understand methods of harvesting fish and apply learning in practice (k, u,s, a, v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners research on and discuss fish farming and aquaponics, the terminology, and the importance of farmed fish to the national diet and to the economy of Uganda. Groups share findings with the class and individuals record conclusions.

In groups, learners research on the characteristics of fresh water fish such as tilapia, carp, trout and other species and record the advantages and disadvantages of each as commercial species, suggesting which they would choose and why.
In pairs, learners investigate local soil and report, giving reasons, verbally or in writing, whether it is suitable for pond construction.

In groups, learners construct a fish pond, a portable fish pond/aquaponics system, or an aquarium at school, and research on the principles for rearing fish in them. Individuals produce a brief guide to successful commercial fish rearing.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners developing practical skills in relation to rearing fish for the market, and provide support to ensure that they make good progress and achieve learning outcomes.
Listen to learners’ conversations and contributions to class discussion. Lead them to further develop their thinking and deepen understanding.

Evaluate the quality of learning through products: reports on terminology and the importance of farmed fish to the diet and the economy; comparisons of different fish species and reasons for choosing one; reports on suitability of soil for pond construction; guides to commercial fish rearing; conclusions on re - stocking; characteristics of a good pond; disease, parasites and predators; learning logs about the rearing process; harvesting, and preservation.
Observe how learners collaborate and negotiate during pond construction and fish rearing.

practicals.title: Fish Pond/Aquarium Construction
practicals.description_verbatim: In groups, learners construct a fish pond, a portable fish pond/aquaponics system, or an aquarium at school, and research on the principles for rearing fish in them.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: know the most important breeds of rabbits, their characteristics, their importance in commercial farming, and their value in nutritional and financial terms (k, a, v, u)
show skills in constructing a rabbit house (s, a, u,v)
understand the safety‘ Dos and Don’ts’ of rabbit-keeping (s, a, v, u)
show skills in feeding, managing, and rearing of rabbits (s, a,v)
show skills in carrying out rabbit health checks (s, a,v)
demonstrate skills of treating diseases and pests in rabbits (a, v, s, k,u)
show skills in processing, marketing of rabbits, and rabbit products (a, v, s, k,u)
show entrepreneurial skills in rabbit rearing (a, v, k,u)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners brainstorm and research on: the important breeds of rabbit and their three commercial uses (meat: Californian, New Zealand, Satin; wool: Jersey, Angora, American; pets: Netherland dwarf, Dutch, Lop) - the value of rabbits in nutritional and financial terms. Groups share findings with the class and individuals record conclusions.
In groups, learners plan, budget, and procure materials for construction of a rabbit house
In groups, learners explore, brainstorm, research on, and record a list of safety ‘Dos and Don’ts’ for rabbits

In pairs, learners manage and rear rabbits, ensuring healthy practice in relation to feeding, watering, housing, grooming, and all aspects of care while keeping individual learning logs of the process.

In groups, learners research on characteristics of a healthy rabbit and demonstrate to the class how to carry out a health check when acquiring a rabbit for rearing (ears are clean, eyes have no discharge/cloudiness, and the nose is clean and dry. The teeth are lined up straight, the front/hind feet have five/four toe nails and are clean at the bottom. The stomach has no abscesses/ discharges, the tail is straight and body condition is clean, smooth, and firm) Individuals record a health checklist
In groups, learners demonstrate and present to class how to treat diseases and pests (like mites, snuffles, and abscesses)
In pairs or individually, learners present a marketing campaign, then proceed to market rabbits and their products

As a class, learners discuss the different entrepreneurial skills needed in rabbit rearing and write a list of the characteristics of an ideal rabbit farmer who earns income. Individuals self-assess against the list.
In groups, learners collect, research on, identify, and draw the different kinds of endo-parasites and ecto-parasites that affect rabbit.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners developing practical skills in relation to rearing rabbits commercially. Provide support to ensure that they make good progress and achieve learning outcomes.

Listen to learners’ conversations and contributions to class, group and pair discussions, leading them to further develop their skills, thinking and deepen understanding of rabbit rearing to earn income.

Evaluate the quality of learning through products: conclusions regarding breeds, their importance in the market, commercial, and nutritional value; rabbit houses; do and don’t lists; learning logs; health checklists; presentations about treatment of pests and diseases and marketing campaigns.
Observe learners’ creativity, collaboration, and risk-taking skills in rabbit rearing.

practicals.description_verbatim: In groups, learners plan, budget, and procure materials for construction of a rabbit house

practicals.title: Rabbit Rearing
practicals.description_verbatim: In pairs, learners manage and rear rabbits, ensuring healthy practice in relation to feeding, watering, housing, grooming, and all aspects of care while keeping individual learning logs of the process.

practicals.title: Rabbit Health Check
practicals.description_verbatim: In groups, learners research on characteristics of a healthy rabbit and demonstrate to the class how to carry out a health check when acquiring a rabbit for rearing

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: identify the breeds of goats reared in Uganda, understand their qualities and the value of goat products in financial and nutritional terms (k, u, a,v)
understand how to choose a goat breed for rearing (u, a,v)
understand the different systems for mating and breeding goats (u, a,v)
show skills in caring for goats, male and female, and kids (u, s, a,v)
show skills in producing and conserving pastures for goats (k, s, a,v)
understand the importance of weaning kids and how to rear them (u, s, a,v)
show skills in processing and marketing of goats and their products (a, v, s, k,u)
show entrepreneurial skills in goat rearing (s, a, u)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners brainstorm and research on the different breeds of goats, their characteristics, and suitability for different products (meat, milk, cheese, skins) as well as the value of these products in financial and nutritional terms. Groups share findings with the class and individuals record conclusions.
In groups, learners use the information to decide an appropriate breed for rearing in the locality and record the reasons for the agreed choice.
In groups, learners manage and rear goats ensuring healthy practice in relation to all aspects of care, and management of pasture. Learners keep individual learning logs of the process

In groups, learners discuss and report on the advantages and disadvantages of different mating and breeding systems for goats, focusing particularly on cross- breeding and pure breeding; assertive mating and random mating

In groups, learners research on and formulate a breeding calendar. Record and be able to tell the age at first mating; including the signs of heat (shaking the tail, mounting, seeking female goats, continuous bleating and mucous discharge at the vulva).
In groups, learners research on and develop a program for rearing kids, including how and when to wean as well as care post-weaning. Individuals complete a report or learning log.
As a class, learners research on, plan, and put into practice a strategy for preparing and conserving hay and silage for goats. Individuals complete a learning log.
In pairs or individually, learners present a marketing campaign and then proceed to market goats and goat products to earn income
As a class, learners discuss the different entrepreneurial skills needed in goat rearing and write a list of the characteristics of an ideal goat farmer. Individuals self-assess against the list.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners developing practical skills in relation to rearing goats commercially and provide support to ensure they make good progress to achieve learning outcomes.
Listen to learners’ conversations and contributions to class, group and pair discussions while asking questions appropriate to further develop their thinking and deepen understanding of goat rearing.

Evaluate the quality of learning through products: conclusions regarding breeds, their importance in the market, and their commercial and nutritional value; breed selections; learning logs; breeding calendars; kid rearing programs; hay and silage strategies and quality of products; marketing campaigns; lists and self-assessments of entrepreneurial skills.
Observe learners’ creativity, collaboration and risk-taking skill in goat rearing

practicals.title: Goat Rearing
practicals.description_verbatim: In groups, learners manage and rear goats ensuring healthy practice in relation to all aspects of care, and management of pasture.

practicals.title: Hay and Silage Preparation

themes.theme_description: Production and marketing of perennial crops.

topics.core_competency: The learner produces and markets perennial crops profitably.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: know the value of coffee/tea / cocoa to the Ugandan economy and the key markets for these products(k, a,v)
understand the general geographical areas in which coffee/tea/cocoa is grown in Uganda and the soil and climatic requirements for propagating and growing (k,u, a,v)
understand how to establish and manage a coffee/tea/cocoa nursery and coffee garden (u,s, a,v)
show skills in applying financial management principles to coffee/tea/ cocoa production (k, s, a,v)
show skills in the preparation of the soil for growing coffee/tea/cocoa seedlings(s, a,v)
show skills in transplanting coffee/tea/ cocoa seedlings into the garden(a, v, s)
show skills in managing coffee/tea/cocoa plants until harvesting(s, a,v)
to harvest and process coffee/tea/cocoa for the market(s, a,v)
roast/cure, grind and serve coffee/tea/ cocoa(s, a, v, u, k)
understand the importance of taste, recognize, and describe the differences in taste and smell as functions in cupping specialty coffees/teas and cocoa(u, a,v)
show entrepreneurial skills in coffee/tea/ cocoa production (s, a, v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: As a class, learners brainstorm and research on the uses and importance of coffee/tea/cocoa to the Ugandan economy, the balance between export destinations and home consumption, and record class conclusions in notes
In pairs, learners carry out research using the library, Internet or other resources, and draw maps showing the geographical locations of where coffee/tea/cocoa is grown in Uganda and in the world

In pairs, learners explore and make notes on the soil and climatic requirement for propagating and growing coffee/tea/ cocoa, and then annotate their maps to explain why the crops are grown in the areas shown
In groups, learners research on (using farm visits, interviews, Internet, and library) how to establish and manage a coffee/tea/cocoa nursery and coffee garden and share conclusions with the class

As a class, learners put the conclusions into practice by preparing the ground, planting, and caring for a coffee/tea/cocoa crop to maximise the harvest. Individuals keep a learning log throughout the process.
In pairs, learners roast/cure, grind and serve coffee/tea/cocoa for the best quality taste and aroma. Individuals further add key learning points to their learning logs.

As a class, learners discuss the different entrepreneurial skills needed in producing coffee/tea/cocoa, and write a list of the characteristics of an ideal coffee/tea/cocoa farmer. Individuals self-assess against the list.

Evaluate the quality of learning through products: conclusions regarding uses and importance of coffee/tea/cocoa crops; maps of growing areas and annotation about climate and soil; conclusions regarding establishment and management of nurseries/gardens; quality of crops harvested; quality of crops after roasting/curing, grinding and quality of drinks served; lists and self-assessments of entrepreneurial skills
Observe learners creatively processing coffee/tea/cocoa, and other post-harvest handling activities.

In pairs, learners carry out research (library, Internet, and local observation/interviews) to select the most appropriate fruit to grow in the locality and report their conclusions to the class.
In groups, learners explore and make notes on the soil and climatic requirement for propagating and growing the fruit selected.
In groups, learners carry out research and visit farmers or processing units to find out about the conditions required to ensure a good quality harvest. Learners record their conclusions.
As a class, learners establish and manage a fruit nursery, growing and caring for the fruit while following appropriate procedures. Individuals keep learning logs of the process.
In pairs, learner’s research on and record the correct methods of grafting, budding, pollarding and pruning fruit trees. Individuals practice and demonstrate skills in each technique.

In pairs, learners read case studies, discuss, and write reports on the correct time and methods of harvesting and marketing fruits such as paw paws, banana (sweet/ cooking), passion fruits, apples, guava, gooseberry and temperate fruits.

Observe learners’ collaboration in growing and marketing of fruits, and tree nursery tending operations.
Observe learners’ attitude in harvesting fruits, pest and disease control, and marketing of fruit products.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: Know the meaning of the terms: agroforestry, watershed, and permaculture. Understand their importance to the environment and value to the Ugandan economy (k,u, a,v)

Understand the rationale for eco-friendly farming techniques in managing and caring for the environment and natural resources. show appropriate skills in agroforestry, watershed, and permaculture development (u,s, a,v)
Design an agroforestry, a watershed and a permaculture model plan for the area (s, a,v)
Understand how to select appropriate tree species and crops for an agroforestry garden, a watershed development area, and a permaculture garden (u,s, a,v)
understand how to establish and manage an agroforestry garden, a watershed development area, and a permaculture garden (u,s, a,v)
show skills in applying financial management principles to planning an agroforestry garden, a watershed development area, and a permaculture garden (k, s, a,v)
know how to harvest and process the products of agroforestry, watershed, and permaculture(k, a,v)
know how to market agroforestry, watershed, and permaculture(k, a, v)
show entrepreneurial skills required to make a success of agroforestry, watershed, and permaculture(s,a)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners brainstorm and research on the meaning, uses and importance of agroforestry, watershed, and permaculture to the Ugandan economy and environment. Share their thoughts with the class. The whole class discusses appropriate areas in the locality for agroforestry, watershed, and permaculture projects in the area. Individuals record conclusions

In pairs, learners: carry out research (library, Internet and other sources ) and select the most appropriate trees and crops for agroforestry, watershed or permaculture projects in the area; design a model plan, explaining the reasons for the decisions about what to plant and where; develop a management plan detailing how to care for both the crops and the environment
As a class, learners grow and care for some selected trees and crops included in the model plan, following appropriate procedures. Individuals keep a learning log.

In groups, learners visit agroforestry farms and/or farms using eco-friendly watershed/permaculture approaches and interview them about management required to ensure a good quality harvest and conservation of the natural environment (If no local examples, theoretical research will be required) Individuals add to learning logs.
In pairs, learners research, read a case study, discuss and report on how to harvest and market products of agroforestry, watershed areas, and permaculture gardens.

As a class, learners discuss the different entrepreneurial and other skills needed in agroforestry, watershed, and permaculture. Learners then write a list of the characteristics of an ideal farmer. Individuals self-assess against the list.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners developing practical skills in relation to planting and growing trees and crops suitable for agro forestry, watershed, and permaculture. Intervene, ask questions and provide support to ensure that they make good progress and achieve learning outcomes.
Listen to learners’ conversations and contributions to pair, group, and class discussion. Ask probing questions and lead them to further develop their thinking and deepen understanding.

Evaluate the quality of learning through products: conclusions regarding the meaning and uses of agroforestry, watershed, and permaculture and suitable locations for projects; model plans and management plans; learning logs; reports on harvesting and marketing of products; lists and self-assessments of entrepreneurship characteristics and other skills.
Observe how learners collaborate, demonstrate creativity and communication, when applying leadership and risk-taking skills.

practicals.title: Growing trees/crops
practicals.description_verbatim: As a class, learners grow and care for some selected trees and crops included in the model plan, following appropriate procedures.

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: Due to the time scales required for growing trees to maturation and the scale of planting required for effective watershed and permaculture systems, the learning activities involved in this unit focus on aspects of practice rather than the whole cycle from planting to harvest (agroforestry), or significant levels of environment-friendly planting (watershed and permaculture).
